text.tspan: The pipeline begins with the raw input image of a scene,
A visual attention model computes a saliency map to identify
the most eye-catching regions of the image.
A thresholding operator, labeled T, uses this saliency map
to split the original image into separate streams.
The upper stream isolates the salient region, representing the user's
primary gaze, while masking out the background.
Dense SIFT features are extracted from this isolated salient region.
These features are then structured using Spatial Pyramid Matching to form
a robust histogram representation of the salient object.
Simultaneously, the lower stream isolates the non-salient region, which captures
the background context or peripheral gist of the scene.
Dense SIFT features are extracted from this peripheral region as well.
A separate Spatial Pyramid Matching histogram is then generated for the non-salient features.
Finally, the salient and non-salient representations are combined and classified
together using a Multiple Kernel Learning Support Vector Machine.
